cause_quote: The commit added the `if (streamPatchRequested && !normalized.streamCommand) { ... return { kind: "patch-existing-stream", ... } }` early return in resolveCronEditScheduleRequest, before the call to resolveDirectSchedule that holds the existing `--on-exit-cwd requires --on-exit.` check.
user_saw: `openclaw cron edit <id> --stream-cwd /x --on-exit-cwd /y` exited 0, changed the stream working directory and silently dropped `--on-exit-cwd`.
summary: Moved the `--on-exit-cwd requires --on-exit` check into normalizeScheduleOptions so it also runs on the stream-metadata edit path.
reasoning: The on-exit-cwd check lived only in resolveDirectSchedule (from the on-exit feature, 68bfa42b) and in create; the stream-metadata edit path that bypasses it was introduced in 98742bc2c7f2 (#112387), whose diff shows the new early return placed before resolveDirectSchedule with the check left in place. The path never validated the flag pair from its introduction, so this is never-worked rather than a regression; later commits only changed error types and trimming.
